# Real-time Collaborative Document Editor in Wasp.sh

## Background

In this task, you will build a full-stack real-time collaborative document editor using Wasp.sh (^0.24.0), React, Node.js, and WebSockets (Socket.IO). Wasp is a full-stack, spec-driven framework where high-level configuration is defined in `main.wasp.ts` using `@wasp.sh/spec`, and data models are defined in `schema.prisma`.

## Requirements

### 1. Authentication & Signup

* Use Wasp's built-in `usernameAndPassword` authentication.
* Map the user's username to the `username` field on the `User` entity during signup using `userSignupFields`.
* Implement a `/signup` page (with `SignupForm` from `wasp/client/auth`) and a `/login` page (with `LoginForm` from `wasp/client/auth`).
* Protect all other routes so that only authenticated users can access them, redirecting to `/login` if unauthenticated.

### 2. Document Management

* Logged-in users can view a list of documents they own or have been shared with on the homepage (`/`).
* Provide a form on the homepage to create a new document. It must have an input field for the document title (`id="document-title-input"`) and a button to submit (`id="create-document-btn"` or text "Create Document").
* Each listed document must link to `/document/:id`.

### 3. Collaborative Editor

* On the document page (`/document/:id`), display the document's title.
* Provide a textarea with `id="document-content-textarea"` for editing the document's content.
* Multiple users must be able to view and edit the same document concurrently. Changes made by any user must be synchronized and reflected in real-time in all other active sessions viewing that document using Wasp's WebSocket integration.
* **Permissions check**:
  * Only the owner, or users with a shared permission ("VIEW" or "EDIT") can access the document page. Other users must see "Access Denied" or be redirected to `/`.
  * If a user has "VIEW" permission, they can only view the document. The textarea (`id="document-content-textarea"`) must be disabled or read-only (`disabled` or `readOnly` attribute present).
  * If a user is the owner or has "EDIT" permission, they can edit the document content. The textarea must be editable.

### 4. Version History

* Users with edit/owner access can save the current document content as a new version. Provide a button with `id="save-version-btn"` or text "Save Version".
* When clicked, it must save the current content as a new `Version` in the database, with the current user as the author, and update the document's primary content.
* Display a list of saved versions in chronological order under `id="version-history-list"`. Each version item must display:
  * The author's username.
  * The version ID or index.
  * A button/link to restore this version with `class="restore-version-btn"` or text "Restore" (only visible to users with edit/owner access).
* Clicking "Restore" must update the document's active content to that version's content and broadcast the change to all other active WebSocket clients immediately.

### 5. Document Sharing (Permissions)

* The document owner (and only the owner) must see a sharing section on the document page.
* Provide an input with `id="share-username-input"` to enter a username, a dropdown/select with `id="share-role-select"` to choose "VIEW" or "EDIT", and a button with `id="share-document-btn"` or text "Share" to share the document.
* Provide a list of users with current permissions under `id="permissions-list"`, including a button to revoke access.

## Implementation Hints

* Project path: `/home/user/app`
* Start command: `wasp start`
* Port: `3000`
* Configuration must be in `main.wasp.ts` and data models in `schema.prisma`.

### Database Schema

Your `schema.prisma` must define the following models:

* `User`:
  * `id`: Int, `@id`, `@default(autoincrement())`
  * `username`: String, `@unique`
  * `documents`: `Document[]` (relation `@relation("DocumentOwner")`)
  * `versions`: `Version[]`
  * `permissions`: `Permission[]`
* `Document`:
  * `id`: Int, `@id`, `@default(autoincrement())`
  * `title`: String
  * `content`: String, `@default("")`
  * `ownerId`: Int
  * `owner`: `User` (relation `@relation("DocumentOwner", fields: [ownerId], references: [id])`)
  * `versions`: `Version[]`
  * `permissions`: `Permission[]`
  * `createdAt`: DateTime, `@default(now())`
  * `updatedAt`: DateTime, `@updatedAt`
* `Version`:
  * `id`: Int, `@id`, `@default(autoincrement())`
  * `documentId`: Int
  * `document`: `Document` (relation `fields: [documentId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade`)
  * `content`: String
  * `authorId`: Int
  * `author`: `User` (relation `fields: [authorId], references: [id]`)
  * `createdAt`: DateTime, `@default(now())`
* `Permission`:
  * `id`: Int, `@id`, `@default(autoincrement())`
  * `documentId`: Int
  * `document`: `Document` (relation `fields: [documentId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade`)
  * `userId`: Int
  * `user`: `User` (relation `fields: [userId], references: [id]`)
  * `role`: String // "VIEW" or "EDIT"
  * `@@unique([documentId, userId])`

### Routing I/O

* `/signup` -> `SignupRoute` (renders `SignupPage` component)
* `/login` -> `LoginRoute` (renders `LoginPage` component)
* `/` -> `RootRoute` (renders `MainPage` component, `authRequired: true`)
* `/document/:id` -> `DocumentRoute` (renders `DocumentPage` component, `authRequired: true`)

**Confirming Import Paths**

I've confirmed that `useParams` is indeed available directly from `"react-router"`, as seen in v7's import conventions. This simplifies our setup considerably.

**Implementing WebSocket Logic**

I'm focusing on integrating WebSocket functionality for real-time document updates. This involves joining document-specific rooms on mount, listening for update and restore events to refresh content, and ensuring proper room departure on unmount. I've drafted initial `useEffect` and `useSocketListener` hooks for this.

**Broadcasting Edits**

I'm refining the document editing flow. I've confirmed emitting `edit-document` with the content and document ID to broadcast changes in real-time. I'm also considering how to best handle database persistence, weighing immediate updates against debouncing for performance.

**Debouncing Database Writes**

I've decided to implement a debounced save mechanism for database updates. This means WebSocket broadcasts will still occur instantaneously with each keystroke for real-time collaboration, but the actual database write will be delayed by a short interval of inactivity to prevent excessive writes and improve performance.

**Refining Initial Content Load**

I'm now considering the nuanced handling of initial document content. The aim is to set the state with fetched content but avoid overwriting user edits, especially when the document refetches. A `useEffect` hook tied to `document.id` changes seems appropriate for this.

**Synchronizing Version Restores**

I'm working through the logic for restoring document versions. The goal is to ensure that when a user restores a version, their local content updates immediately, and this change is broadcast to all other connected clients. This update should also trigger a database write. The key is to make sure subsequent refetches don't interfere with active typing.

**Implementing Version Controls**

I'm now focusing on the versioning feature. This involves creating a "Save Version" button, persisting new versions to the database with the current user as author, and updating the document's primary content. I'm also setting up a chronological list of saved versions, each with author details and a restore option.

**Designing Page Layout**

I'm now focusing on the visual structure of `DocumentPage.tsx`. I have successfully implemented the Real-time Collaborative Document Editor in Wasp.sh (^0.24.0). 

Here is a summary of the implementation details:

### 1. Database Schema (`schema.prisma`)
Defined the following models with all relationships and requirements:
* **User**: Represents the user, holding authentication fields, owning documents, authoring versions, and holding permissions.
* **Document**: Holds the document metadata and core content. Includes references to the owner (`User`), lists of `Version` history, and `Permission` records.
* **Version**: Holds historical snapshots of document content, referencing the parent `Document` and the authoring `User`.
* **Permission**: Controls access and roles (`VIEW` or `EDIT`) for shared users.

### 2. Configuration & Routing (`main.wasp.ts`)
* Configured full-stack authentication using built-in `usernameAndPassword` with `userSignupFields` to map the username during signup.
* Configured WebSockets (`webSocket`) with `autoConnect: true` and linked it to the server-side handler.
* Registered the routes:
  * `/signup` -> `SignupRoute` (renders `SignupPage`)
  * `/login` -> `LoginRoute` (renders `LoginPage`)
  * `/` -> `RootRoute` (renders `MainPage` with `authRequired: true`)
  * `/document/:id` -> `DocumentRoute` (renders `DocumentPage` with `authRequired: true`)
* Declared queries and actions with automated entity tracking.

### 3. Server-side Operations & Hooks
* **Signup Mapping (`src/auth/signup.ts`)**: Implemented `userSignupFields` mapping to capture and save the username during registration.
* **WebSocket Handler (`src/websocket.ts`)**: Handles real-time room joining (`join-document` / `leave-document`), real-time content synchronization (`edit-document` / `document-updated`), and real-time version restoration broadcasts (`restore-document` / `document-restored`).
* **Queries (`src/queries.ts`)**:
  * `getDocuments`: Returns all documents owned by or shared with the authenticated user.
  * `getDocument`: Retrieves a document, checking permissions and resolving the user's role (`OWNER`, `EDIT`, or `VIEW`).
* **Actions (`src/actions.ts`)**:
  * `createDocument`: Creates a new document owned by the authenticated user.
  * `updateDocumentContent`: Persists content changes (with permissions checks).
  * `saveVersion`: Updates active content and saves a historical snapshot.
  * `restoreVersion`: Reverts active content to a historical snapshot.
  * `shareDocument`: Grants `VIEW` or `EDIT` permissions to another user.
  * `revokePermission`: Revokes shared access.

### 4. Client-side Pages & Components
* **Authentication Pages (`src/pages/auth/LoginPage.tsx` & `SignupPage.tsx`)**: Render `LoginForm` and `SignupForm` with links to navigate between pages.
* **Main Dashboard (`src/MainPage.tsx`)**: Lists accessible documents and displays the creation form with `id="document-title-input"` and `id="create-document-btn"`.
* **Document Page (`src/DocumentPage.tsx`)**:
  * Displays title, active content, and role.
  * Synchronizes editing in real-time using `useSocket` and `useSocketListener` from `"wasp/client/webSocket"`.
  * Implements high-performance **debounced database auto-saving** on typing, combined with **instant WebSocket broadcasts** for lag-free collaboration.
  * Restricts editing of `id="document-content-textarea"` (using `disabled`) if the user has `VIEW` permissions.
  * Displays version history under `id="version-history-list"`, with a save button (`id="save-version-btn"`) and restore buttons (`className="restore-version-btn"`).
  * Provides a sharing sidebar (`id="share-username-input"`, `id="share-role-select"`, `id="share-document-btn"`, and `id="permissions-list"`) for the owner to manage permissions.

The database migrations have been successfully executed and the application is running smoothly with the server listening on port `3001` and client on port `3000`.
